q01.key_idea: Count the kangaroo's jumps, and move the rabbit the same number of times.
steps: The kangaroo starts at the bottom. The rabbit starts on step 10.
The kangaroo goes up 3 steps at a time: 3, 6, 9. So it moves 3 times to reach step 9.
Each time, the rabbit goes down 2 steps: 10, 8, 6, 4.
After 3 moves the rabbit is on step 4.

choice_feedback.A: The rabbit stops on 8, 6, 4. It never stops on step 3.
choice_feedback.C: The rabbit stops on 8, 6, 4. It never stops on step 5.
choice_feedback.D: The rabbit is on step 6 after only 2 moves, when the kangaroo is on step 6, not 9.
choice_feedback.E: The rabbit stops on 8, 6, 4. It never stops on step 7.

q02.key_idea: A piece that covers another piece was put on the table later.
steps: The pentagon lies on top of everything, so it went on last.
The white triangle covers the long rectangle, and the rectangle covers the black circle.
The black circle covers the left edge of the square, so the square is at the very bottom.
From the bottom up: square, circle, rectangle, triangle, pentagon. The second piece is the circle.

choice_feedback.A: The triangle was the fourth piece. It lies on the rectangle.
choice_feedback.B: The square was the first piece, at the very bottom.
choice_feedback.D: The rectangle was the third piece. It lies on the circle.
choice_feedback.E: The pentagon was the last piece, on top of all the others.

q03.key_idea: In the photo the car must look the same as in the picture, with Marco standing in front of it.
steps: Look at the car: its smile and its small eye are on the right side.
In A, B and D the car faces the other way, with the smile on the left.
In C the car faces the right way, but Marco stands on top of the car, not in front of it.
In E the car faces the right way and Marco stands in front, covering part of the smile.

choice_feedback.A: The car faces the other way, and Marco is peeking out from behind the car.
choice_feedback.B: The car faces the other way: its smile is on the left.
choice_feedback.C: Marco is standing on top of the car, not in front of it.
choice_feedback.D: The car faces the other way, and its eyes are green.

q04.key_idea: The coins he won must be the same as the coins he paid.
steps: Try 2 right days: he wins 3 + 3 = 6 coins.
Then 5 - 2 = 3 days are wrong: he pays 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 coins.
He won 6 and paid 6, so he has the same coins as at the start.

choice_feedback.A: With no right days he pays 2 coins 5 times, so he loses 10 coins.
choice_feedback.B: He wins 3 coins but pays 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 coins, so he loses coins.
choice_feedback.D: He wins 9 coins and pays only 4, so he gains coins.
choice_feedback.E: He wins 12 coins and pays only 2, so he gains coins.

q05.key_idea: The animals come in groups of 5, so count in fives.
steps: The order is: mouse, snail, yellow bird, frog, red bird. Then it starts again.
Animals 5 and 10 are both red birds, at the end of a group.
Animal 11 is a mouse, 12 is a snail, 13 is a yellow bird and 14 is a frog.

choice_feedback.C: The snail is animal 12, not 14.
choice_feedback.D: The yellow bird is animal 13, not 14.
choice_feedback.E: The red bird is animal 15, not 14.

q06.key_idea: Count each shape on the cards and in the tower, then see what is left over.
steps: The cards have 6 circles, 5 squares and 6 triangles.
The tower has 5 circles, 5 squares and 4 triangles.
Left over: 6 - 5 = 1 circle, 5 - 5 = 0 squares and 6 - 4 = 2 triangles.

choice_feedback.A: All 5 squares are in the tower, so no square is left over.
choice_feedback.B: All 5 squares are in the tower, and a circle is left over.
choice_feedback.D: No square is left over, and 2 triangles are left over, not 1.
choice_feedback.E: 2 triangles are left over, not just 1.

q07.key_idea: Find how many white cubes there are in all, then take away the white cubes you can see.
steps: The block is 4 cubes long, 3 cubes high and 2 cubes deep: 12 + 12 = 24 cubes.
Half of them are white, so there are 12 white cubes.
White cubes you can see: 5 on the front, 3 more on top of the back row, and 2 more on the right side of the back row. 5 + 3 + 2 = 10.
12 - 10 = 2 white cubes are hidden.

choice_feedback.A: You can see 10 white cubes, so 12 - 10 = 2 are hidden, not 1.
choice_feedback.C: Count the white cubes you can see again: there are 10, so only 2 are hidden.
choice_feedback.D: Remember the white cubes on top and on the right side of the back row. Only 2 are hidden.
choice_feedback.E: You can see 10 of the 12 white cubes, so only 2 are hidden.

q08.key_idea: Count the squares and the triangles in each drawing. A square turned on its corner is still a square.
steps: A: 3 squares, 2 triangles. B: 3 squares, 3 triangles. C: 3 squares, 3 triangles.
D: 2 squares, 3 triangles. E: 4 squares, 3 triangles.
Only D has fewer squares than triangles: 2 is less than 3.

choice_feedback.A: It has 3 squares and only 2 triangles, so it has more squares.
choice_feedback.B: It has 3 squares and 3 triangles, the same number.
choice_feedback.C: It has 3 squares and 3 triangles, the same number.
choice_feedback.E: It has 4 squares and 3 triangles, so it has more squares.

q09.key_idea: Look at what sits in the 4 corners of each tile, then find that tile in the wall.
steps: Each tile has something in its corners: an orange petal, a pink point or a green corner.
Tile A is the middle tile of the bottom row. Tile B is the middle tile of the top row.
Tile C is the second tile of the top row. Tile D is the tile in the bottom right corner.
Tile E has orange petals in both top corners. No tile in the wall has 2 orange petals side by side, even if you turn it.

choice_feedback.A: This is the middle tile of the bottom row.
choice_feedback.B: This is the middle tile of the top row.
choice_feedback.C: This is the second tile from the left in the top row.
choice_feedback.D: This is the tile in the bottom right corner of the wall.

q10.key_idea: Find the streets that have only 2 houses. The new house must sit on all of them.
steps: Count the houses on each street. Most streets already have 3 houses.
The straight street from the top left to the bottom right has only 2 houses, both in its top left part.
The biggest circle has only 2 houses: one on the far left and one on the far right.
Point D is where that straight street meets the biggest circle, so one house there fixes both streets.

choice_feedback.A: A is on the straight street across the middle, which already has 3 houses.
choice_feedback.B: B is on the straight street going up and down, which already has 3 houses.
choice_feedback.C: C is on the straight street across the middle, which already has 3 houses.
choice_feedback.E: E is on the straight street from the top right to the bottom left, which already has 3 houses.

q11.key_idea: Count the cubes in each block, including cubes that are only partly seen.
steps: A: a tower of 3 cubes, 1 cube beside it and 1 cube in front. 3 + 1 + 1 = 5.
B has 6 cubes: a middle cube with 1 on top, 1 on each side and 2 in a row in front.
C and D each have 7 cubes, and E has 8 cubes.
5 is the smallest number.

choice_feedback.B: B has 6 cubes. Look for the cube hiding between the middle cube and the front cube.
choice_feedback.C: C has 7 cubes, counting the one peeking out at the back.
choice_feedback.D: D has at least 7 cubes, counting the one peeking out at the back.
choice_feedback.E: E has 8 cubes: 6 on the bottom and 2 more stacked up.

q12.key_idea: Add the front flower, double it, then see what the back flower is missing.
steps: Front flower: 5 + 3 + 1 + 9 + 7 = 25.
The back flower must add up to twice that: 25 + 25 = 50.
The petals we can see on the back flower: 4 + 6 + 2 + 8 = 20.
The hidden petal is 50 - 20 = 30.

choice_feedback.A: Then the back flower adds up to 25, the same as the front flower, not twice as much.
choice_feedback.B: Then the back flower adds up to 32, not 50.
choice_feedback.C: Then the back flower adds up to 45, not 50.
choice_feedback.E: Then the back flower adds up to 60, not 50.

q13.key_idea: The face that touches 4 of the other faces is opposite the face we never see.
steps: The first cube shows the red square, the star and the triangle. The second cube shows the triangle, the circle and the arrow.
The triangle is on both cubes, so it touches the square, the star, the circle and the arrow.
A face touches 4 faces and is opposite just 1. The only face left is the sixth face, the one we never see.
So the triangle is opposite that sixth face.

choice_feedback.A: The circle is one of the 4 faces around the triangle, and those 4 faces all touch the sixth face.
choice_feedback.C: The star is one of the 4 faces around the triangle, and those 4 faces all touch the sixth face.
choice_feedback.D: The arrow is one of the 4 faces around the triangle, and those 4 faces all touch the sixth face.
choice_feedback.E: The square is one of the 4 faces around the triangle, and those 4 faces all touch the sixth face.

q14.key_idea: Every 3 squares in a row add to 10, so the numbers repeat every 3 squares.
steps: Squares 1, 2, 3 add to 10, and squares 2, 3, 4 also add to 10.
Both groups share squares 2 and 3, so square 4 must be the same as square 1.
Square 1 has a 2, and the gray square is square 4. So the gray square gets 2.

choice_feedback.A: The gray square must hold the same number as the first square, which is 2, not 1.
choice_feedback.C: The gray square must hold the same number as the first square, which is 2, not 3.
choice_feedback.D: The gray square must hold the same number as the first square, which is 2, not 4.
choice_feedback.E: The gray square must hold the same number as the first square, which is 2, not 8.

q15.key_idea: Turning over the right side gives the same picture as turning over the top side and then spinning it halfway around.
steps: In the picture we see, the skateboard is at the top, the head is at the bottom and the tail points left.
Turning the card over its right side instead is like turning it over the top and then spinning it upside down.
Spinning halfway around moves the skateboard to the bottom, the head to the top and the tail to the right.
Picture D shows the kangaroo like that.

choice_feedback.A: The skateboard is at the bottom, but the tail still points left. It is a mirror picture.
choice_feedback.B: The skateboard is still at the top. Only the tail moved to the right.
choice_feedback.C: This is the same picture we get by turning over the top side.
choice_feedback.E: This kangaroo is turned on its side.

q16.key_idea: Give each grandchild as many cupcakes as possible, then see what is left.
steps: 6 grandchildren with 3 cupcakes each use 6 + 6 + 6 = 18 cupcakes.
With 4 each, she would need 24 cupcakes, but she has only 23.
So each gets 3, and 23 - 18 = 5 are left for Grandma.

choice_feedback.A: Then she would share 22 cupcakes, but 22 can't be shared equally among 6 children.
choice_feedback.B: Then she would share 21 cupcakes, but 21 can't be shared equally among 6 children.
choice_feedback.C: Then she would share 20 cupcakes, but 20 can't be shared equally among 6 children.
choice_feedback.D: Then she would share 19 cupcakes, but 19 can't be shared equally among 6 children.

q17.key_idea: Check what the row and the column of the colored box still need.
steps: The colored box is in the bottom row and the right column.
The right column already has a card with 2 squares, and the bottom row has a card with 1 square. So the box can't have squares.
The right column already has a 2 and the bottom row already has a 1. So the box needs 3 shapes.
Among the cards to choose from, only the card with 3 circles has 3 shapes that are not squares.

choice_feedback.A: It has squares, and the right column already has squares.
choice_feedback.B: It has 1 shape, and the bottom row already has a card with 1 shape.
choice_feedback.C: It has 2 squares, but the right column already has squares and a 2.
choice_feedback.D: It has 1 square, but the bottom row already has a square and a 1.

q18.key_idea: When one train's wagon number goes up by 1, the other train's number goes down by 1.
steps: Wagon 7 is side by side with wagon 12.
The trains face opposite ways. Move one wagon along: one number goes up by 1 and the other goes down by 1.
So wagon 8 is side by side with wagon 11. Check: 7 + 12 = 19 and 8 + 11 = 19.

choice_feedback.B: 10 + 11 = 21, but the pairs always add to 7 + 12 = 19.
choice_feedback.C: 11 + 11 = 22, but the pairs always add to 19.
choice_feedback.D: Wagon 12 is next to wagon 7, not wagon 11.
choice_feedback.E: 15 + 11 = 26, but the pairs always add to 19.

q19.key_idea: Count all the dark chocolates, then take away the dark square ones.
steps: Half of 14 is 7, so 7 chocolates are dark.
Among the square ones, only 2 are not white, so 2 square chocolates are dark.
The other dark ones are round: 7 - 2 = 5.

choice_feedback.A: 2 is the number of dark square chocolates, not round ones.
choice_feedback.B: Then there would be only 3 + 2 = 5 dark chocolates, but there are 7.
choice_feedback.C: Then there would be only 4 + 2 = 6 dark chocolates, but there are 7.
choice_feedback.E: Then there would be 6 + 2 = 8 dark chocolates, but there are only 7.

q20.key_idea: Each pair of opposite faces has the same sum, and all six numbers must be different and at most 9.
steps: We see 4, 5 and 8. The faces opposite them are hidden.
Try 3 opposite 8: 8 + 3 = 11. Then 4 needs 7 and 5 needs 6, because 4 + 7 = 11 and 5 + 6 = 11.
The numbers 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 are all different and all from 1 to 9. It works!

choice_feedback.B: 5 is already on another face, and each number is used only once.
choice_feedback.C: 8 + 6 = 14, so 4 would need 10. That is too big.
choice_feedback.D: 8 + 7 = 15, so 4 would need 11. That is too big.
choice_feedback.E: 8 + 9 = 17, so 4 would need 13. That is too big.

q21.key_idea: Seat the 4 girls without a boy first, then fill the other tables with a boy and a girl.
steps: The 4 girls without a boy sit 2 at a table, so they fill 2 tables.
14 - 2 = 12 tables are left. Each has 1 boy and 1 girl.
Girls: 12 at the boy-girl tables plus the 4 others. 12 + 4 = 16.

choice_feedback.A: That is too few: 12 girls already sit with boys.
choice_feedback.B: That is too few: 12 girls already sit with boys.
choice_feedback.C: 12 girls sit with boys, but you must add the 4 girls without a boy.
choice_feedback.D: 14 is the number of tables, not the number of girls.

q22.key_idea: Add up all four sides. Each colored corner gets counted twice.
steps: Each side adds to 13, so the four sides together make 13 + 13 + 13 + 13 = 52.
The numbers 1 to 8 add up to 36. That counts every circle once.
In the 52, each colored corner is counted twice, once for each of its sides. So the colored circles add up to 52 - 36 = 16.

choice_feedback.A: The colored circles must make up the extra 52 - 36 = 16, not 12.
choice_feedback.B: 13 is the sum of one side, not the sum of the colored circles.
choice_feedback.C: The colored circles must make up the extra 52 - 36 = 16, not 14.
choice_feedback.D: The colored circles must make up the extra 52 - 36 = 16, not 15.

q23.key_idea: The tallest person has no arrow going out, because nobody is taller than them.
steps: An arrow goes from the shorter person to the taller one.
Arrows leave A, B, D, E and F, so each of them is shorter than someone.
No arrow leaves C, and the arrow from D points to C. So C is taller than D.
Everyone else leads to D by following the arrows, so C is the tallest.

choice_feedback.A: Person A has an arrow going to D, so A is shorter than D.
choice_feedback.B: Person B has arrows going to A and to F, so B is shorter than both.
choice_feedback.D: Person D has an arrow going to C, so D is shorter than C.
choice_feedback.E: Person E has an arrow going to D, so E is shorter than D.

review.note: Data problem: every choice text is just 'Person' with the letter missing; the explanation assumes choice X means person X. The figure also has a sixth person F who is not a choice. With that reading the arrows confirm key C (person C is tallest).

q24.key_idea: Count all the ways to pick 3 white houses, then take away the ways that leave Maia stuck.
steps: There are 6 white houses. Each one touches A's pink houses at the bottom left or B's pink houses at the top right.
Maia gets across when two colored white houses touch each other, one touching A's pink houses and one touching B's pink houses.
There are 20 different ways to pick 3 of the 6 white houses.
Only 4 picks leave Maia stuck: the 3 white houses next to A's pink houses, the 3 next to B's pink houses, and 2 more picks with a gap in the middle. 20 - 4 = 16.

choice_feedback.A: Only 4 of the 20 picks leave Maia stuck, so 16 picks work, not 15.
choice_feedback.C: Check again: 4 picks leave Maia stuck, not 3.
choice_feedback.D: Check again: 4 picks leave Maia stuck, not 2.
choice_feedback.E: Not every pick works: 4 of the 20 picks leave Maia stuck.
